body:
## Summary
- rename the repo env var to `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_DEFAULT_KEY` to match Supabase's generated setup snippet

The repo previously documented and read `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, while Supabase's generated setup flow uses `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_DEFAULT_KEY`. Renaming the repo variable removes that mismatch and makes the onboarding path line up with what developers copy from Supabase.

title: fix(docs): Correct README clone URL and directory to circlefin/arc-nanopayments
body:
## Summary

The README's "Getting Started" section references both an internal repository name and a stale directory name in the clone command, which returns 404 for new contributors:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/akelani-circle/arc-nanopayments-demo.git
cd arc-nanopayments-demo
```

The correct public repository is `circlefin/arc-nanopayments` and the `cd` path should match. This blocks the entire setup flow on the very first step.

## Change

```diff
-git clone https://github.com/akelani-circle/arc-nanopayments-demo.git
-cd arc-nanopayments-demo
+git clone https://github.com/circlefin/arc-nanopayments.git
+cd arc-nanopayments
```

## Verification

```bash
$ git ls-remote https://github.com/akelani-circle/arc-nanopayments-demo.git
ERROR: Repository not found.

$ git ls-remote https://github.com/circlefin/arc-nanopayments.git
✅ resolves
```

## Related

The same `akelani-circle/...` pattern was identified across other Arc sample apps and addressed in:

- [`arc-fintech#9`](https://github.com/circlefin/arc-fintech/pull/9) by @skyc1e
- [`arc-escrow#16`](https://github.com/circlefin/arc-escrow/pull/16) by me
- [`arc-p2p-payments#9`](https://github.com/circlefin/arc-p2p-payments/pull/9) by me

This PR completes the same minimal fix across the public Arc sample app repositories.

## Notes

- This is a documentation-only change (1 file, +2/-2).
- Note that this repo's case is slightly worse than the others both the org (`akelani-circle` → `circlefin`) and the repo name (`arc-nanopayments-demo` → `arc-nanopayments`) need correcting, hence the `cd` line also changes.

title: fix: increase maxTimeoutSeconds to 7 days and surface verification failure reason
body:
## Problem

Two issues that together make the demo non-functional out of the box:

### 1. All payments fail with `authorization_validity_too_short`

`maxTimeoutSeconds` is set to `345600` (4 days). The hosted Circle Gateway facilitator currently enforces a minimum authorization validity window longer than 4 days, so **every payment is rejected** on the signed retry. The agent only prints a generic `Payment failed: Payment verification failed` with no indication of why.

I discovered this by running the demo end-to-end and adding logging to surface the facilitator's actual response — the rejection reason is `authorization_validity_too_short`.

### 2. Verification failure reason is swallowed

`verifyResult.invalidReason` is returned by the facilitator but never logged server-side, making it invisible to developers debugging payment failures.

## Fix

1. Bumped `maxTimeoutSeconds` from `345600` → `604800` (7 days). Payments verify and settle immediately after this change.
2. Added a `console.error` that logs `invalidReason` when verification fails, so any future policy changes surface immediately instead of appearing as a generic failure.

## How to reproduce (before fix)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/circlefin/arc-nanopayments.git
cd arc-nanopayments
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local
# fill in wallets + Supabase
npm run dev
npm run agent
# Result: every request shows "Payment failed: Payment verification failed"
```

title: fix: remove orphaned duplicate balanceInterval in agent.mts
body:
## Summary
  Removes a duplicate/orphaned `balanceInterval` in `agent.mts`.

  ## Bug
  At startup, `balanceInterval` is assigned once right after the initial
  deposit (`balanceInterval = setInterval(checkAndRedeposit, 30_000);`), and
  then `startPaymentLoop()` is called immediately after, which assigns
  `balanceInterval` again to a **new** interval. The first interval's handle is
  overwritten before it's ever cleared, so it keeps running for the lifetime of
  the process with no way to cancel it.

  Net effect: `checkAndRedeposit` actually runs on two overlapping 30s
  schedules instead of one (contradicting the comment above it), and one
  `setInterval` handle leaks for the life of the CLI process.

  ## Fix
  Removed the premature top-level assignment. `startPaymentLoop()` already
  sets up `balanceInterval` (and is the single place that creates/clears it
  across pause/resume cycles triggered by `handleLimitReached()`), so nothing
  else needs to schedule it beforehand.

  ## Testing
  Read-through / static verification — traced every assignment and
  `clearInterval` call site for `balanceInterval` in `agent.mts` to confirm
  `startPaymentLoop()` is the only place that should own it, and that this was
  the sole leaked reference. No functional change to the deposit/payment logic
  itself, only the interval bookkeeping.

Discovered while studying the repo as a reference for building a live payment system on Arc.

The README describes the payment agent (`agent.mts`, run via `npm run agent`) as an

title: fix: require shared secret for withdraw endpoint (#29)
body:
## Problem

`POST /api/gateway/withdraw` has no authentication. It moves the seller's Gateway balance using `SELLER_PRIVATE_KEY` and accepts an arbitrary `destinationAddress`, so anyone who can reach the endpoint can drain the seller's funds to their own wallet:

```bash
curl -X POST https://<host>/api/gateway/withdraw \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"amount":"100","destinationChain":"arcTestnet","destinationAddress":"0xAttacker..."}'
```

## Fix

Adds an **optional** shared-secret guard in `app/api/gateway/withdraw/route.ts`, right after the `SELLER_PRIVATE_KEY` check. When `WITHDRAW_SECRET` is set, every request must present a matching `x-withdraw-secret` header or it is rejected with `401 Unauthorized`:

```ts
const withdrawSecret = process.env.WITHDRAW_SECRET;
if (withdrawSecret) {
  const provided = req.headers.get("x-withdraw-secret");
  if (provided !== withdrawSecret) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, { status: 401 });
  }
}
```

The guard is opt-in so it does not break the existing demo flow when the secret is unset — but the default is now documented as unsafe for production, giving operators a clear, secure path.

## Why not wire the secret through the frontend?

The only caller is `components/dashboard/withdraw-dialog.tsx`, a **client component** running in the browser. Injecting the secret there would require `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, which ships it in the client bundle and defeats the purpose. This guard is therefore intended for **server-to-server or env-gated use**; the README recommends calling the endpoint from a trusted server-side context for hosted deployments. There is no existing session/auth middleware in the repo to reuse.

## Changes

- `app/api/gateway/withdraw/route.ts` — optional `x-withdraw-secret` guard
- `.env.example` — `WITHDRAW_SECRET=` with a warning that leaving it unset exposes the endpoint
- `README.md` — "Protecting the withdraw endpoint" note under Security & Usage Model

## Testing

`npm run build` passes (route compiles and builds; the endpoint is server-rendered on demand).

Closes #29

title: Fix payment verification: facilitator requires 7-day authorization validity
body:
## Problem

Running the demo as documented (`npm run dev` + `npm run agent`) fails on every payment:

```
#1 quote FAILED: Payment failed: Payment verification failed
```

Circle's hosted batch facilitator now rejects burn-intent authorizations valid for less than **7 days** with `authorization_validity_too_short`. This repo signs 4-day authorizations (`maxTimeoutSeconds: 345600`), matching the pinned `@circle-fin/x402-batching` v2.0.4 — but the facilitator-side requirement has since moved (SDK v3.x uses `GATEWAY_MIN_AUTH_VALIDITY_SECONDS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60` plus a 100s buffer).

The failure reason was also invisible: the server returned `invalidReason` in the 402 body but never logged it.

## Fix

- Bump `maxTimeoutSeconds` to `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 + 100`. The client derives `validBefore` from the server's payment requirements, so this single server-side change fixes both sides of the flow.
- Log the facilitator's `invalidReason` on verification failure so this class of error is diagnosable from server logs.

## Verification

90-second soak test on Arc Testnet after the change: **78/78 payments settled, 0 failures** across all 4 premium endpoints at 1 tx/s (quote $0.001, dataset $0.01, compute $0.0003, agent-task $0.03).

title: Fix: Harden local environment secrets, lazy Supabase initialization and strict withdrawal input validation
body:
### Description
This PR addresses local credential leaks, build-time initialization crashes, financial API contract vulnerabilities, and supply-chain dependencies in the `arc-nanopayments` repository.

**Vulnerabilities & Security Defects Remediated:**
* **Secrets and Local File Protection (`generate-wallets.mts`):** Wallet generation previously printed raw private keys to stdout and created environment files without restrictive permissions. The script now outputs only the file path to the console and enforces strict file permissions (`0600` via `writeFileSync` options and `chmodSync`) when persisting generated keys to `.env.local`.
* **Runtime Configuration and Build Safety (`lib/x402.ts`, `app/api/gateway/withdraw/route.ts`):** Supabase clients were previously instantiated during top-level module evaluation using non-null assertions, causing `next build` to fail whenever deployment secrets were absent. The clients are now created lazily inside `getSupabaseClient()` at request time, throwing explicit runtime errors only when payment or withdrawal persistence is actively executed.
* **API Contract and Financial Input Validation (`app/api/gateway/withdraw/route.ts`):** The POST withdrawal endpoint previously accepted unchecked JSON payloads, non-finite or negative transfer amounts, and unvalidated destination addresses. The handler now enforces strict validation:
  * Validates that the request body is a valid JSON object.
  * Enforces string field types and verifies that `amount` is a finite positive number.
  * Validates EVM destination addresses against a strict hex regex (`^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$`).
  * Enforces own-property membership checks (`Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty`) against supported gateway domains.
  * Verifies the presence of a successfully inserted database withdrawal record before invoking external Gateway API methods.
* **Dependency & Supply-Chain Security (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`):** Updated direct dependencies to patched releases (`next` and `eslint-config-next` to `16.3.2`, `postcss` to `8.5.26`, `deepagents` to `1.13.1`, and `viem` to `2.55.19`) to resolve known advisories across the dependency tree.

title: Authentication, Input Validation, and Fault Tolerance Hardening in `arc-nanopayments`
body:
### Description
This pull request introduces critical security remediations across the `arc-nanopayments` service[cite: 20]. The primary vulnerability addressed is the total absence of boundary enforcement (F1)—previously, any unauthenticated caller could reach the `/dashboard` and `/api/gateway/*` paths, including the USDC withdrawal signer[cite: 20]. This patch implements secure HMAC-SHA256 session tokenization, extracts hardcoded secrets into secure environment variables, validates payload constraints on EVM addresses and withdrawal amounts, strictly processes currency in exact-precision `BigInt` formats, and correctly handles external API service outages using robust "fail-closed" mechanics[cite: 20].

### Key Changes & Remediations

#### 1. Authorization Boundaries & Session Integrity (F1)
* **Middleware Route Enforcement (`middleware.ts`, `lib/auth.ts`):** Established an explicit enforcement boundary for `/dashboard` and `/api/gateway/*`[cite: 20, 39]. Operator sessions were previously authenticated by a predictably static "authenticated" cookie string that the application never actually verified[cite: 20, 39]. The token is now a robust HMAC-SHA256-signed payload featuring absolute 8-hour expiry validation[cite: 20, 39]. 

#### 2. Secrets & Configuration Management (F2)
* **Removed Hardcoded Credentials (`app/actions.ts`):** Operators previously authenticated using globally visible hardcoded credentials (`admin@example.com` / `123456`)[cite: 20, 39]. This logic has been rewritten to extract and securely map `ADMIN_EMAIL` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD_SHA256` environment configurations using constant-time digest verification[cite: 20, 39].

#### 3. Input Validation & Web3 Withdrawals (F3)
* **Secure Payment Signatures (`app/api/gateway/withdraw/route.ts`):** 
  * The USDC withdrawal gateway (which authorizes payouts using the `SELLER_PRIVATE_KEY`) previously blindly accepted unauthenticated requests featuring arbitrary addresses and uncapped withdrawal values[cite: 20].
  * Added mandatory session validation, `MAX_WITHDRAWAL_USDC` thresholds (capped at 10,000 USDC), and rigorous hex-format EVM address verification on the `destinationAddress` parameter[cite: 20, 39]. 
  * Addressed object injection risks in `destinationChain` checks by verifying the value strictly via `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(GATEWAY_DOMAINS, ...)` rather than loose attribute access[cite: 20, 39].

#### 4. Numeric Precision & Arithmetic Safety (F4)
* **BigInt Scaling (`lib/x402.ts`):** Monetary prices translated to Atomic Units were previously susceptible to floating-point truncation corruption (e.g., `Math.round(parseFloat(price) * 1_000_000)`)[cite: 20, 39]. The conversion was re-implemented using exact `BigInt` mappings that safely throw errors rather than silently evaluating to `NaN` when malformed price inputs arise[cite: 20, 39]. Note: the `USDC_SCALE` is built dynamically utilizing `BigInt(10) ** BigInt(6)` to satisfy the project's rigid `ES2017` compiler target requirement[cite: 20, 39].

#### 5. Reliability & Fault Tolerance (F5, F6)
* **Fail-Closed Balance Checks (`app/api/gateway/withdraw/route.ts`):** Mitigated silent fallback execution bugs during balance verification queries[cite: 20, 39]. Network/RPC failures across `getBalances()` now enforce a strict "Fail Closed" design returning HTTP 503 rather than suppressing errors and continuing to withdrawal[cite: 20, 39].
* **Observability & Error Propagation (`lib/x402.ts`):** Improved payment settlement handling in `withGateway`[cite: 20, 39]. Failures happening *after* funds have moved are now explicitly tracked with detailed `PAID BUT UNFULFILLED` console logs preventing blind external exposure of unhandled raw exceptions[cite: 20, 39].

## Validation
* **Byte-Compilation (`npx tsc --noEmit`):** Executed and completed seamlessly inside `arc-nanopayments` (Exit 0)[cite: 20]. The `TS2737` BigInt literal constraints were resolved, ensuring backwards compatibility against ES2017 transpilation architectures[cite: 20].

title: fix(x402): add Idempotency-Key replay guard to withGateway
body:
## Summary
Fixes #43

`withGateway()` verified and settled every request independently: a client that timed out waiting for the 402 → settle round trip and re-issued the same logical request caused a **second, independent settlement** for the same purchase. Gateway's own nonce handling only protects byte-for-byte signature replays — each retry attempt carries a fresh payment signature, so it settles again.

### Changes
- Read an optional `Idempotency-Key` header (behavior unchanged when absent)
- After `verify()` (payer known), before `settle()`: look up a successful `payment_events` row for the same `(endpoint, payer, key)` within a 24h window; on hit, rebuild `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` from the stored row and **skip `settle()` entirely**
- Persist the key on the `payment_events` insert so replays are durable across restarts and instances
- Migration: nullable `idempotency_key` column + partial unique index on `(endpoint, payer, idempotency_key)`

### Limitations (stated honestly)
- Sequential retries (the common timeout-retry case the issue describes) are fully covered
- Two truly concurrent requests with the same key can still race past the check-before-settle; the partial unique index makes the second `insert` fail loudly rather than double-record, but cannot un-settle the first transfer. A claim-before-settle pattern (admission row inserted before `settle()`) would close that too, at the cost of a more invasive schema change — happy to follow up if wanted

### Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- `eslint . clean
- No test infra exists on `master` for `lib/x402.ts` (vitest arrives with other open PRs); logic is straightforward check-before-settle

title: fix: add idempotency guard to withGateway()
body:
## Summary

Fixes #43: `withGateway()` had no replay/idempotency defense — a caller stuck in a retry loop could settle multiple independent payments for the same logical request.

## Changes

- `lib/x402.ts`: added `Idempotency-Key` header support with in-memory cache (24h TTL)
- Repeat requests with the same key by the same payer for the same endpoint return the cached result with no second settlement call
- Cache key derived from `(payer, endpoint)` using SHA-256

## Impact

This repo is Circle's own canonical nanopayments reference implementation, so the gap would get copy-pasted into every app that follows this pattern.
